brand.name: Lucas
brand.line: Computer science student in Singapore. I build Telegram bots and websites.

bot.welcome: I study computer science at NTU in Singapore and build Telegram bots and websites for small businesses. This bot is one of them: everything you tap here is something I can build for you.

paragraphs: I am a second-year computer science student at NTU in Singapore. Outside lectures I build small software systems for businesses: Telegram bots, websites, and the databases that connect them.

Before university I interned at a networking company, configuring switches and VLANs and helping move an office to a new internet provider, and I taught myself the CCNA syllabus. During National Service I worked as a finance clerk, handling logistics and procurement.
I also tutor part-time, which is how I came to build a matching system for a tuition agency. I like software that stays lean: few moving parts, and nothing to maintain that does not need maintaining.
Away from the screen it is tennis (I was vice-captain of my junior college team), the gym, basketball and pickleball.

projects.name: Tutor-matching system for a tuition agency
projects.summary: A Telegram bot, a database and a live assignments page for a Singapore home tuition agency. The owner posts an assignment once and it reaches the website, the channel and every tutor it fits. Tutors register, browse and apply inside the bot.
projects.stack: Telegram Bot API · PostgreSQL · serverless functions · 34 automated tests

projects.name: Finance tracker
projects.summary: The tracker I use for my own money: transactions, recurring bills, CSV import, holdings with live prices and travel spending in other currencies. It holds four years of my records.
projects.stack: HTML, CSS and JavaScript · Chart.js · runs in the browser

projects.name: Website, bot and channel as one program
projects.summary: The page you are reading, its Telegram bot and its channel all run from one small program. The form at the bottom lands in my Telegram, and the channel posts on a schedule without me.
projects.stack: Node.js · Telegram Bot API · no third-party libraries

process.name: Brief
process.text: Tell me what you need through the bot or the form. I reply within one working day with questions or a quote.

process.name: Fixed quote
process.text: You get the scope, price and delivery date in writing. A 50% deposit starts the build.

process.name: Build
process.text: You get a working preview within days and test it on your own phone. Changes inside the scope are included.

process.name: Launch and handover
process.text: I deploy it, hand over the accounts and a short guide, and the fix period starts.

faq.q: Do I need to know anything technical?
faq.a: No. You tell me what the bot or site should do in plain words. At handover you get a short guide for the few things you will change yourself, such as prices and text.

faq.q: Who owns the bot and the code?
faq.a: You do. The bot is registered under your Telegram account, the domain is in your name, and you get the source code at handover.

faq.q: Where does it run, and what does that cost?
faq.a: On a small cloud server, usually a few dollars a month. You can pay the host directly, or the care plan covers hosting and monitoring.
Yes. Telegram supports payments through providers such as Stripe, and a bot can also send a payment link and confirm when it is paid.

faq.q: How long does a project take?
faq.a: A starter bot or landing page takes about a week from deposit. Larger builds take two to four weeks. The date is in your quote.

faq.q: What if I need changes after launch?
faq.a: Fixes are free during the fix period in your package. After that, the care plan covers small edits and larger changes are quoted separately.

perk.text: Channel members get 10% off their first project.
